summary: Extract the direct-limit multiplicative-perfection and rationalized Picard-groupoid mechanisms, geometric pushouts, finite-relation and proper-group-action quotients, semiampleness gluing and the exact mixed-characteristic Keel and threefold applications. Preserve all representability, characteristic-zero-fiber, excellence and residue-field guards. Reuse existing invertible sheaves, scheme morphism properties and abstract filtered colimits; do not confuse Mathlib's inverse-limit Perfection with this paper's direct limit. Source diagnostics and unfinished original-input proof closure keep this a partial checkpoint.

items.name: Nef abundant numerical-dimension-one surface bundle
items.statement: On a normal projective surface over an algebraically closed field, a nef line bundle with numerical dimension1 and Iitaka dimension1 is semiample.
items.locator: Guarded input for Corollary6.7; compare Keel99 Lemma5.2
items.note: Proof supplied by the continuation of Claude Code (cc-fb70e5, 22 September 2026). It is characteristic-free and uses only Mumford intersection theory on normal surfaces, base-point-freeness of a moving pencil with M²=0, Stein factorization and Zariski's lemma. This closes gap-surface-nef-repair for this item. surface-rr-growth still carries that gap for its Riemann–Roch input.
proofSteps: Let L be nef on a normal projective surface S over an algebraically closed field (any characteristic), with L²=0 and κ(L)=1. Choose m with h⁰(mL)≥2 and write |mL|=|M|+F, with M the moving part and F≥0 the fixed part. M is nef, since |M| has no fixed component. Intersections of Weil divisors use Mumford's theory.
Since L is nef, 0=m L²=L·M+L·F with both terms ≥0, so L·M=L·F=0. Then M²=mL·M−M·F=−M·F≤0 and M²≥0, so M²=0 and M·F=0. Finally F²=mL·F−M·F=0.

|M| is base-point-free: two general members have no common component and intersection M²=0, and local intersection numbers of distinct curves on a normal surface are positive at common points, so they are disjoint. Since κ(L)=1, φ_{|M|} has one-dimensional image. Its Stein factorization f:S→C has connected fibres, and M=f*A with A ample on the normal projective curve C.

M·F=0 with M=f*A nef forces every component of F to be f-vertical. Group F=Σ_tF_t by fibres; distinct fibres are disjoint, so F²=ΣF_t². By Zariski's lemma the intersection form on the components of the connected fibre G_t=f*(t) is negative semidefinite with kernel QG_t, so each F_t²≤0. Hence F_t²=0 and F_t=q_tG_t with q_t∈Q_{≥0}, as divisors.

Choose k>0 clearing the denominators of the q_t. Then kmL∼kM+kF=f*(kA+Σ_t kq_t[t]), where kA+Σkq_t[t] has positive degree and is ample on C. So some power of L is a pullback of a very ample divisor, and L is semiample.

Scope: the bare hypothesis "ν(L)=1 and h⁰(L^m)>0" is insufficient (diagnostic D5 gives a ruled-surface counterexample with κ=0). Corollary 6.7 supplies κ=1 through the linear growth of χ(mL) and the H² bound (surface-rr-growth and surface-h2-bound).
